contribution_method: LightGBM tree SHAP via pred_contrib=True — days relative to the model's base value

chirps.name: CHIRPS v2.0 daily (UCSB Climate Hazards Center)

backtest: leave-one-year-out, all districts of a year held out together
label_note: Labels are the v2 onset rule — 5-day rainfall ≥ local Jun–Sep mean (2001–2025), no break ≥ 10 days under 5 mm — applied to CHIRPS v2.0 (UCSB Climate Hazards Center) daily rainfall over DOY 121–270. Labels and the rainfall feature come from the same product, so this is a same-source nowcast check; no comparison against a third rainfall dataset has been run.

sources.weather_features: NASA POWER daily point series (T2M, T2M_MAX, RH2M, GWETROOT)
sources.indices: NOAA PSL ONI (ERSSTv6 3-month running mean) and DMI (HadISST1.1)
sources.power_rainfall_excluded: POWER PRECTOTCORR is not used for labels or the rainfall feature in the CHIRPS arm: at Tangail its annual total averages 937 mm in 1981–1996, 1714 mm in 1997–2015 and 2814 mm in 2016–2025, so a 45-year anomaly climatology would be measuring the product, not the monsoon. The POWER arm is therefore reported for 2001–2025 only.
sources.power_weather_note: Temperature, humidity and root-zone moisture also come from a reanalysis-merged product; they are used as anomalies against each fold's own climatology, which limits but does not remove the same inhomogeneity risk.
sources.chirps_grid: CHIRPS v2.0 is a 0.25° daily grid: a point's value is its nearest cell, not a station reading.

out_of_sample.note: One season only, and only where the v2 rule could already confirm the onset; it is not evidence of skill on its own.

farm_district_note: A demo farm's baseline and prior-season onset come from the district it sits in; its own 1 Mar – 20 Apr rainfall comes from its own CHIRPS cell.
onset_rule: Onset definition v2 (local-relative 5-day accumulation, adapted from Moron & Robertson 2014)
issue_before_onset: The outlook is issued on 25 April. The v2 window opens at DOY 121 (1 May in 2026), so in some districts the real onset falls only days after the issue date: the model predicts an event that can arrive almost immediately, not one a season away.
